newsitem.title: JAPAN: US has repeatedly asked Japan for fiscal steps - MOF.
newsitem.headline: US has repeatedly asked Japan for fiscal steps - MOF.

text.p: Finance Minister Wataru Kubo told a news conference on Friday that the U.S. authorities have repeatedly asked Tokyo to take fiscal and monetary steps to support Japan's economic recovery.

"In various meetings, the U.S. Treasury has told us that it is important for Japan to take fiscal and monetary steps to support the economic recovery and prevent it from losing steam," Kubo said. He said he considered the U.S. views important, but it was up to Japan to decide economic policy.

He was replying to a question about a report in a Japanese newspaper on Friday which said that when U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers met Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of MOF's International Finance Bureau, earlier this month, the U.S. expressed concern over Japan's economic recovery.

Kubo said the government would like to decide what measures could be taken for the economy after looking at gross domestic product (GDP) figures for the April-June quarter to be released on Friday afternoon.

He said he would also like to take into account the economic prospects for the coming months in deciding the steps and added that the decision would likely be made sometime next week. Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said earlier this month he would like to decide whether to draw up a supplementary budget with economic stimulus measures after the release of the GDP figures.
